title: Make the celery visibility_timeout redelivery docs version-conditional
body:
Three doc surfaces describe a broker redelivery as terminating the
still-running original task:

- the `[celery] task_acks_late` config description in `provider.yaml` (and its
  generated mirror in `get_provider_info.py`), which also describes the failure
  as surfacing only as `'Task Instance Not Running' FAILED: Task is in the running state'`
- the runtime warning from `_broker_transport_options` when no
  `visibility_timeout` is configured
- `celery_executor.rst`, which asks for a visibility timeout above the longest
  task ETA without saying what happens if it is not

That stopped being the only outcome in `apache-airflow-providers-celery` 3.18.0
(#64052): `celery_executor_utils` raises `Ignore()` on
`TaskAlreadyRunningError`, so the redelivered message is discarded and the
original task keeps running. It also needs Airflow 3.1.9 or newer, because the
409 it relies on comes from the Execution API and the provider still gates on
`AIRFLOW_V_3_1_9_PLUS` — so the existing text remains correct below that floor
and is now scoped to those versions rather than replaced.

Measured on Airflow 3.3.2 with provider 3.24.0: a 301-second task under a
60-second visibility timeout reached `success`, and the duplicate logged
`Task already running elsewhere, ignoring redelivered message`.

Neither surface named a version floor, and the provider doc set had a single
bullet about visibility timeout with no explanation of the mechanism, so this
adds a "Visibility timeout and long-running tasks" section covering
`task_acks_late`'s interaction with redelivery, both version floors, and SQS's
43200-second cap.

Follow-up to #62869, which added the warning text. It was accurate for the
provider versions available at the time; this PR scopes it to those versions.

### Validation

- `providers/celery/tests/unit/celery/executors/test_celery_executor.py`: 81 passed, 18 skipped
- `get_provider_info.py` regenerated from `provider.yaml`, byte-identical to the committed file
- `provider.yaml` passes both the provider schema and the runtime `provider_info` schema
- ruff check/format, mypy, yamllint, codespell clean on the changed files
- new prose checked against hunspell en_US plus `docs/spelling_wordlist.txt`

Sphinx docs build not yet run locally; I am relying on the CI `build-docs` job
for the new RST section and its cross-reference.

 Some caveats:
 
 - Make sure to use a database backed result backend

+- Make sure to set a visibility timeout in ``[celery_broker_transport_options]`` that exceeds the ETA of your longest running task (see `Visibility timeout and long-running tasks`_)
 - Make sure to specify the password for Redis Server in the ``[celery_broker_transport_options]`` section if you are using Redis Sentinel as your broker and the Redis servers are password-protected
 - Make sure to set umask in ``[worker_umask]`` to set permissions for newly created files by workers.
 - Tasks can consume resources. Make sure your worker has enough resources to run ``worker_concurrency`` tasks
 - Queue names are limited to 256 characters, but each broker backend might have its own restrictions
 
+Visibility timeout and long-running tasks
+-----------------------------------------
+
+Brokers that redeliver unacknowledged messages -- Redis and Amazon SQS -- hide a delivered message for
+``[celery_broker_transport_options] visibility_timeout`` seconds. Because ``[celery] task_acks_late``
+is enabled by default, a message is acknowledged only once its task finishes, so any task that runs
+for longer than the visibility timeout is redelivered while it is still running.
+
+Setting ``task_acks_late`` does not prevent this. For Redis and SQS it does not override
+``visibility_timeout``: the broker redelivers the message regardless.
+
+Both deliveries carry the same Celery task id, so a failure reported for the redelivery cannot be
+told apart from one reported for the original task.
+
+With ``apache-airflow-providers-celery`` 3.18.0 or newer running on Airflow 3.1.9 or newer, the
+redelivered message is detected and discarded. The worker logs ``Task already running elsewhere,
+ignoring redelivered message``, and the original task runs to completion. Both version floors are
+required: the provider recognizes the condition, but it relies on the Execution API behavior added
+in Airflow 3.1.9.
+
+On earlier versions the redelivery terminates the still-running original task, which surfaces only as
+``'Task Instance Not Running' FAILED: Task is in the running state``.
+
+Set ``visibility_timeout`` to exceed the ETA of your longest running task. Note that Amazon SQS caps
+the visibility timeout at 43200 seconds (12 hours), so on SQS it cannot be raised any further and
+tasks running for longer than 12 hours are always redelivered.
+
